tagline: Rangsit at the end of the train line, canal-side rice fields, theme parks, and a big science museum
introHtml:
Pathum Thani sits just north of Bangkok. Hop on the SRT Red Line or head out along Vibhavadi–Phahonyothin and you're there. Most people think of Rangsit and Future Park first, but once you turn off into the canals you'll find temples, rice fields, markets, and big museums all mixed together.

This is a university and residential province. You've got Thammasat Rangsit, Dream World theme park, the National Science Museum complex out at Khlong Ha, and traces of old Mon riverside communities along the Chao Phraya. It makes an easy day trip from Bangkok.
bestTime: November–February, cool and dry with little rain — good for walking around outdoors and heading out to the fields all day

highlights.name: Rangsit & Future Park
highlights.blurb: The commercial heart of the province, anchored by the big Future Park Rangsit mall at the end of the SRT Red Line — restaurants, food, and things to do all close together

highlights.name: Dream World
highlights.blurb: A long-running theme park near Khlong Sam with rides and photo zones. It's a family favorite that Bangkok folks drive out to for a full day

highlights.name: National Science Museum, Khlong Ha
highlights.blurb: A cluster of science, natural history, and information-technology museums, marked by its tilted cube building. Kids can wander through it all day

highlights.name: Wat Chedi Hoi
highlights.blurb: A temple in Lat Lum Kaeo where giant oyster fossils millions of years old were dug up. There's a shell-fossil museum and a quiet rice-field setting

highlights.name: Sam Khok Mon Community
highlights.blurb: An old district on the Chao Phraya that still keeps its Mon heritage — old temples, pottery, and the Sam Khok water jars it was once known for

highlights.name: Talad Thai
highlights.blurb: A huge wholesale fruit and vegetable market in Khlong Luang, open almost round the clock. It's where Central Thailand buys fresh produce at wholesale prices

foodScene.name: Rangsit Boat Noodles
foodScene.note: Rangsit is boat-noodle territory — small bowls with a deep, rich broth, and several old shops where you order several at a time

foodScene.name: Khao Chae & Mon Sweets
foodScene.note: The Sam Khok area still has Mon-style food and sweets, from khao chae in the hot season to local treats at temple fairs

foodScene.name: Canal-side Dining
foodScene.note: Restaurants along Khlong Rangsit and the Chao Phraya serve freshwater fish, prawns, and made-to-order dishes with a waterside feel

foodScene.name: Field & Canal Cafes
foodScene.note: Around Khlong Luang, Khlong Sam, and Lam Luk Ka there are plenty of new cafes with rice-field and waterside views to sit and relax

foodScene.name: Eats Around the Universities
foodScene.note: The Thammasat Rangsit area and the campuses around Khlong Luang are packed with student spots — rice plates, moo kratha, and milk tea

foodScene.name: Moo Kratha & Grill Buffets
foodScene.note: Lam Luk Ka and Rangsit have loads of moo kratha and grill buffet places — a go-to dinner for groups of friends and families

foodScene.name: Fruit & Fresh Produce at Talad Thai
foodScene.note: Talad Thai is the place for seasonal fruit at wholesale prices — stop in for durian, mango, and fresh vegetables to take home

foodScene.name: Rangsit Market Street Food
foodScene.note: Rangsit Market and the nearby night markets have plenty of food to graze on — fried snacks, sweets, and one-plate dishes

attractions.name: Dream World
attractions.blurb: A theme park near Khlong Sam with rides, a snow zone, and photo corners — good for the whole family

attractions.name: National Science Museum (NSM)
attractions.blurb: A cluster of science and natural-history museums at Khlong Ha, with hands-on exhibits where kids can play and learn by doing

attractions.name: Wat Chedi Hoi
attractions.blurb: A Lat Lum Kaeo temple that displays prehistoric giant oyster fossils, set among rice fields and a small farm

attractions.name: Golden Jubilee Museum of Agriculture
attractions.blurb: An agriculture museum off Phahonyothin Road at Khlong Nung, with rice paddies, farm gardens, and a farmers' market on weekends

attractions.name: Wat Sing, Sam Khok
attractions.blurb: An old temple on the Chao Phraya in the Sam Khok Mon community, with a historic ordination hall and a quiet riverside setting

attractions.name: Rahaeng 100-Year-Old Market
attractions.blurb: An old canal-side market in Lat Lum Kaeo, with wooden shophouses, local snacks, and an old-time feel on weekends

attractions.name: Thep Pathum Park
attractions.blurb: A riverside public park in central Pathum Thani, with a waterfront plaza, a walking track, and shady trees to relax under

attractions.name: Khlong Rangsit & Khlong Luang Rice Fields
attractions.blurb: The Khlong Rangsit canal and the rice fields around Khlong Luang–Lam Luk Ka — good for driving around to find cafes and field-view photo spots
